_note: The story that opens every reading, in The Völva's register: silly, and exact. It is assembled from these lines by the chart: who sent you (the Atmakaraka), the costume (the rising sign, or the Sun's sign when the birth time is unknown), the gift and its shadow (the Moon's mansion, its shakti from corpus.json), and the houseguests (the Vimshottari periods, with the ages they arrive). Placeholders in curly braces are filled in by the site; keep them. Change any line and every reading changes with it.
TITLE: Prologue: How You Got Here
SUB: a silly story, and a true one; the rest of the reading decodes it
OPENING: Before you were born{named} you stood in the queue at the Well of Urðr — the three Norns at the root of the World Tree, spinning. The queue was long. The person ahead of you was contesting their Moon; contesting your Moon never works. Then it was your turn.
NAMED: , before anyone called you {name} (that came later, and was not your idea),
SOUL_INTRO: Urðr keeps what has already happened, which is to say she keeps the ledger. She found your page, and on it the name of whoever had sent you.

SOUL.Sun: The Sun had sent you — and the Sun does not send quietly. Pinned to your coat: THIS ONE IS TO SHINE. You have been trying to take the note off ever since. It does not come off. The errand: to become entirely yourself, in public.
SOUL.Moon: The Moon had sent you, with provisions and far too much feeling. The errand: to look after people. You took it literally. The footnote, which you skipped: you are one of the people.
SOUL.Mars: Mars had sent you — by throwing. The errand was scratched on the back of a shield: do the brave thing. Underneath, smaller: stop asking whether it is the brave thing.
SOUL.Mercury: Mercury had sent you, talking the whole way down. The errand: a message to deliver. No one mentioned that you would have to understand it first, or that it would keep changing in your hands.
SOUL.Jupiter: Jupiter had sent you — generously, and with a reading list. The errand: to find out what is true. The small print: and then, regrettably, to teach it.
SOUL.Venus: Venus had sent you, after a long discussion about the outfit. The errand: to love something properly — all the way through, including the parts that bore you. Especially those.
SOUL.Saturn: Saturn had sent you, eventually, once the paperwork cleared. The errand: to build something that lasts. Saturn issued you the slow way on purpose; it does not trust the fast way, and it has seen what the fast way builds.

COSTUME_INTRO: Verðandi keeps what is happening now, so it fell to her to take you to the dressing room. Twelve rails of costumes. You chose {costume}.
COSTUME_UNKNOWN: (No one wrote down the minute you came through the door, so the costume is read from your Sun's sign. It fits anyway — costumes here are tailored after the fact.)

COSTUME.Aries: a helmet one size too big, visor already up, already dented by something you have not yet done
COSTUME.Taurus: a heavy velvet cloak and very good boots — chosen for comfort, and you have refused to be hurried out of either since
COSTUME.Gemini: two costumes, because choosing one was out of the question; you wear them on alternate days, and on the difficult ones, at once
COSTUME.Cancer: a shell — hard outside, soft within, with deep pockets for other people's things
COSTUME.Leo: a mane, a crown and a small portable spotlight, none of which you remember ordering and all of which you kept
COSTUME.Virgo: a pressed apron with a sewing kit in the pocket, in case anything in the universe needed mending — something always does
COSTUME.Libra: something beautiful that went with everyone else's, chosen after polling the whole queue
COSTUME.Scorpio: a long dark coat with an inside pocket no one else has seen into
COSTUME.Sagittarius: travelling clothes, a bow, and boots already muddy from somewhere you have not been yet
COSTUME.Capricorn: a sensible coat that looks nine hundred years old — because it is, and it still fits
COSTUME.Aquarius: something no one had worn before, which several people in the queue said would never catch on
COSTUME.Pisces: a costume made almost entirely of water: beautiful, and very hard to keep on

GIFT: Before you left, Verðandi packed the gift. On the label: {mansion}. Inside: {shakti} — the old books call it {shakti_name}. Then, being exact, she folded the shadow into the same bag. A gift and its misuse travel together; that is the arrangement. You found the shadow later. Everyone does.
TIMING_INTRO: Skuld, the youngest, keeps what shall be — the appointment book. No one is born into an empty house. One planet is always in residence; the rest arrive in turn, stay for years, and move the furniture.
FIRST: When you arrived, someone was already in the house: {visitor}. They stayed until you were {age}.
FIRST_BRIEF: When you arrived, someone was already in the house, coat on, leaving: {visitor}. Gone before your first birthday.
NOW: That is who is in the house now.

VISITOR.Ketu: Ketu — no luggage, moves nothing, and leaves you certain you have done all this before
VISITOR.Venus: Venus, who stays twenty years, redecorates, and brings the people you will love
VISITOR.Sun: the Sun — brief, bright, and asking what you have actually made of yourself
VISITOR.Moon: the Moon, who rearranges the furniture of your feelings and calls it tidying
VISITOR.Mars: Mars, already running, who needs a project, a fight, or both
VISITOR.Rahu: Rahu — hungry; wants more of everything, and most of whatever was forbidden
VISITOR.Jupiter: Jupiter, with teachers, children, luck, and a long talk about meaning
VISITOR.Saturn: Saturn, who stays nineteen years and has you do it properly this time
VISITOR.Mercury: Mercury — the trade, the talk, the study, and the endless lists

CLOSING: That is how you got here. A silly story — and every word of it true in the way that matters. The costume is The Seat. The gift and its shadow are The Engine. Whoever sent you is The Soul-Planet. The houseguests, and when they come, are The Clock. What follows is the decoder.
